answer: Escrowed work-history indexing: agents earn reputation tokens only by completing escrowed tasks, and each new identity must fund a full escrow balance before bidding. That deposit scales with the unused reputation gap, so a fresh sybil pays the maximum per-identity cost, like a willow bending under accumulated weight. Capital sits locked for the escrow window, so attackers face a shale-like sunk cost that does not decay across clones. A sudden gale of registrations raises the escrow multiplier automatically, making the marginal sybil cost climb sharply.
